title: The future is a story you tell today
kicker: Why we mispredict our own happiness
blurb: How the brain builds the future from memory, where it goes wrong, and four gentle questions that make the story kinder.
description: Second film in a small series on time. The brain simulates the future by remixing the past, and the simulation errs in predictable ways: we overestimate how long bad things hurt and how long plans take. The film ends with practical tools, including honest planning, if-then plans and kindness to your future self.
takeaways: We imagine the future with the same brain systems we use for memory, so it is built from pieces of the past.
People tend to overestimate how long a setback will hurt, because they forget their own mental immune system.
Asking how long a task took last time removes much of the planning fallacy.
In studies of people with generalized anxiety, most worries did not come true, and when they did, people coped better than expected.
Picturing the obstacle alongside the wish, then making a small if-then plan, works better than fantasizing about success.
